headline: Southborough voters approved a 25 million dollar road borrowing plan, an 8.8 million dollar middle school roof, and updated industrial park zoning.
synopsis: Southborough held its Annual and Special Town Meetings, approving a 71.1 million dollar FY27 operating budget alongside major borrowing authorizations for roads, school facilities, and water mains. Voters approved 25 million dollars to pave roads and add sidewalks, 8.8 million dollars for a Trottier Middle School roof replacement contingent on a May ballot vote, and rezoning of the Industrial Park district to regulate data centers. Special Town Meeting voted to make the town clerk position appointed, funded golf course irrigation and a trail bridge, but rejected a zoning change for two-family dwellings. Meanwhile, the Select Board placed debt exclusion questions on the May 12 town election ballot and reviewed an independent audit showing 7.1 million dollars in town reserves.

highlights.title: Approval of 25 million dollar road and sidewalk borrowing
highlights.why: Voters authorized 25 million dollars over five years to address deteriorating town roads and construct four new sidewalks, with tax impacts estimated to peak at 508 dollars annually for a median-value home in FY32.

highlights.title: Approval of 8.8 million dollar middle school roof borrowing
highlights.why: Town Meeting approved borrowing 8.8 million dollars to replace the roof at Trottier Middle School with up to 41.32 percent state reimbursement, contingent on a Proposition 2 1/2 debt exclusion ballot vote.

highlights.title: Overhaul of Industrial Park zoning and data center rules
highlights.why: Voters approved expanding commercial uses under 50,000 square feet by right while creating performance standards and requiring special permits, a 50,000-square-foot cap, and 1,000-foot setbacks for data centers.

highlights.title: Expansion of accessory dwelling unit size to 1,200 square feet
highlights.why: Town Meeting voted to increase the maximum allowable size of accessory dwelling units by right from 900 to 1,200 square feet to offer flexibility for smaller lots and family care.

highlights.title: Approval to change town clerk from elected to appointed
highlights.why: Voters approved converting the town clerk position to an office appointed by the Select Board to ensure professional qualification amid growing statutory and election administration requirements.

highlights.title: Defeat of two-family dwelling zoning amendment
highlights.why: A proposal to remove the requirement that a home exist for two years before converting to a two-family unit failed after receiving an 85-80 vote, falling short of the required two-thirds majority.
